newsitem.title: ITALY: Lower Italy rates seen helping output - study.
newsitem.headline: Lower Italy rates seen helping output - study.

text.p: Italian manufacturing output is likely to show a one percent fall for 1996 but the outlook for 1997-98 is positive with industry turnover expected to increase due to lower interest rates and financial charges, a study said.
The report, by research group Prometeia and analysts at Banca Commerciale Italiana, forecast a return to growth this year with manufacturing output up 2.0 percent, followed by 3.0 percent in 1998.
It said the scenario discounted the inclusion in spring 1998 of Italy in the first wave of single European currency members.

"In a system of fixed exchange rates the major effects will be from interest rate changes," the study said, forecasting a fall in rates paid by companies on their short-term debt to below 7.0 percent next year.
This fall in loan rates would eliminate one of the causes of the decline in industrial production in 1996 when firms were paying real rates of sometimes over 13 percent, the study said.

While high rates of interest led to a drawdown in stocks last year, a further factor depressing output was the sharp decline in exports of manufactured goods due to the lira's appreciation and weakness of European markets.

However, "thanks to a recovery in demand from EU countries, exports of manufactured goods should increase in 1997-98 by 4.9 percent and 6.4 percent respectively, against just a 3.9 percent rise in 1996," the report said.
Companies' operating costs should remain contained due in part to a lack of pressure on global commodity prices, a maintained incomes policy and an expected increase in productivity, it added.
